Hannah / team —

Thanks for the tag. Quick legal guidance:

- Authority: For purchase commitments >= $1M we require either (a) a named authorized signatory on letterhead or (b) a signed POA that explicitly grants signing authority for the Order Form. A copy of the signer's org chart or procurement authorization is acceptable if procurement policies use delegated limits.
- Execution mode: Sequential DocuSign routing (customer first) is fine and preserves the audit trail. If Delta wants embedded signing, include the redirect/return URL and we will bake that into the envelope config.
- Notarization / witness: Not needed in most US transactions, but if your internal procurement policy requires witness or notarization for high-value orders please flag now.
- Signature block: Please ensure the signer's block includes full printed name, title, and a company name line that matches Delta Health LLC. We will reject signers where the company name is abbreviated/omitted.

I've attached a short "signature-authority-checklist.pdf" that Delta can fill and return. Once we receive confirmation of the named signer (or PoA), Hannah can create the DocuSign envelope and include the final clean PDF.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
